answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because knoll only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, lagoon is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any dawn approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
